hero.title: Ace Your Phone Screen
hero.subtitle: 50% of senior candidates fail at this stage
hero.description: The phone screen is your first real interaction with the company. For senior roles, it's not just about technical competency - they're evaluating your communication, leadership signals, and whether you're worth bringing to the expensive on-site loop. This guide shows you exactly what to prepare.

whatIsPhoneScreen.title: What is the Phone Screen?
whatIsPhoneScreen.subtitle: The critical first filter in your interview journey
whatIsPhoneScreen.overview: The phone screen (or video screen) is typically 45-60 minutes with a recruiter, hiring manager, or senior team member. For senior roles (L6+), expect deeper probing on your leadership experience, scope of impact, and cultural fit. This is where most experienced professionals stumble - they treat it like a casual chat instead of a structured interview.

keyFacts.label: Duration
keyFacts.description: Typically one session, sometimes split into recruiter + technical

keyFacts.label: Interviewer
keyFacts.description: Hiring Manager, Senior Engineer, or dedicated phone screener

keyFacts.label: Format
keyFacts.description: Mix of experience discussion, role fit, and light technical probing

keyFacts.label: Pass Rate
keyFacts.description: Only 1 in 3 senior candidates advance to the loop

stages.name: Intro & Rapport Building
stages.focus: Your background, why this role, why this company
stages.tips: Have a crisp 2-minute pitch ready. Don't ramble. Show genuine interest in the specific role.

stages.name: Experience Deep Dive
stages.focus: Your most impactful projects, leadership experience, scope of work
stages.tips: Prepare 3-4 STAR stories that showcase leadership at scale. Quantify everything.

stages.name: Technical Assessment
stages.focus: Domain knowledge, system design thinking, problem-solving approach
stages.tips: For managers, expect questions on architecture decisions, team scaling, and technical strategy.

stages.name: Role Fit & Questions
stages.focus: Why you want this role, your questions about the team and challenges
stages.tips: Ask thoughtful questions that show you've researched the role. Avoid generic questions.

roleSpecificPrep.title: Phone Screen by Role
roleSpecificPrep.subtitle: Each role has unique evaluation criteria

roles.title: Engineering Manager / Sr. Engineering Manager
keyQuestions: Tell me about your largest team and how you structured it
How do you balance technical work with people management?
Describe a time you had to make a difficult hiring or firing decision
How do you handle underperforming team members?
What's your approach to technical strategy and roadmap planning?
commonMistakes: Not having clear metrics for team success

roles.title: SRE Manager / Sr. SRE Manager
keyQuestions: How do you define and measure reliability for your systems?
Tell me about an outage you managed and what you learned
How do you balance reliability work with feature development?
What's your approach to on-call culture and burnout prevention?
How do you drive adoption of SRE practices across engineering?
mustDemonstrate: Automation and toil reduction at scale
commonMistakes: Focusing only on firefighting, not prevention
Missing the people management aspect of SRE leadership

roles.title: Production Manager / Technical Program Manager
keyQuestions: Describe the most complex program you've delivered
How do you manage dependencies across multiple teams?
Tell me about a time a program was at risk and how you saved it
How do you communicate status to executives?
What's your approach to risk identification and mitigation?
commonMistakes: Not having specific examples of saving at-risk programs
Over-focusing on process instead of outcomes

roles.title: Director of Engineering
keyQuestions: How do you build and scale an engineering organization?
Tell me about a time you drove a major technical transformation
How do you set technical strategy for your organization?
Describe how you manage managers and develop leaders
How do you balance short-term delivery with long-term technical investments?
commonMistakes: Talking like a senior manager instead of an executive
Not having a clear org-building philosophy

roles.title: VP of Engineering
keyQuestions: How do you align engineering strategy with business objectives?
Tell me about building an engineering culture at scale
How do you make build vs. buy decisions?
Describe your approach to M&A integration from an engineering perspective
How do you manage through organizational change and uncertainty?
commonMistakes: Sounding too tactical instead of strategic
Not connecting engineering to business outcomes
Missing the culture and people aspects

roles.title: Principal/Staff Architect
keyQuestions: Tell me about the most complex system you've designed
How do you influence technical decisions across teams you don't own?
Describe a time you had to deprecate a major system
How do you balance innovation with reliability?
What's your approach to mentoring senior engineers?
mustDemonstrate: System design at massive scale (millions of users)
Communication of complex ideas to non-technical stakeholders
commonMistakes: Only talking about individual systems, not org-wide impact

commonQuestions.title: Universal Phone Screen Questions
commonQuestions.subtitle: These come up in almost every senior phone screen

questions.question: Walk me through your background
questions.what_they_want: A crisp 2-minute narrative showing career progression and increasing scope
questions.tip: End with why THIS role at THIS company is the natural next step

questions.question: Why are you looking to leave your current role?
questions.what_they_want: A positive, forward-looking answer (not complaints about current employer)
questions.tip: Focus on growth opportunities, not escape from problems

questions.question: Tell me about your biggest accomplishment
questions.what_they_want: A high-impact story with clear metrics showing leadership and scale
questions.tip: Use STAR format. Quantify the impact. Show YOUR specific contribution.

questions.question: What's your management/leadership philosophy?
questions.what_they_want: A clear, articulate framework for how you lead
questions.tip: Have 3-4 principles you can explain with examples

questions.question: Tell me about a failure and what you learned
questions.tip: Pick a real failure, own it, and show how you changed

questions.question: Why this company? Why this role?
questions.tip: Reference specific things about the company's mission, challenges, or products

questions.question: What questions do you have for me?
questions.what_they_want: Thoughtful questions showing you've done homework
questions.tip: Ask about team challenges, success metrics, and strategic priorities

flags.why: Senior leaders must communicate concisely. If you can't do it in an interview, how will you do it in exec meetings?
Shows poor judgment and potential cultural issues
Senior roles require metrics-driven thinking. 'Made things better' isn't enough.
Shows lack of interest or preparation
For leadership roles, they want to see how you lead and multiply impact through others
Basic research is expected. Not knowing signals you're mass-applying.

preparation.title: How to Prepare
preparation.subtitle: Do this before every phone screen

steps.title: Research the Company
activities: Read recent news and press releases
Understand the product and business model
Look up the interviewer on LinkedIn

steps.title: Prepare Your Stories
activities: Write out 4-5 STAR stories covering key competencies
Ensure each story has quantified impact
Practice saying each story in 2-3 minutes
Have a 'failure' story ready with genuine learning

steps.title: Prepare Your Pitch
activities: End with why this role is the right next step
Practice until it sounds natural, not rehearsed

steps.title: Prepare Your Questions
activities: Include questions about team challenges and success metrics
Avoid questions about compensation or benefits at this stage

steps.title: Technical Prep
activities: Be ready to explain your technical decisions at a high level
Know your systems' architecture and trade-offs
Prepare for light coding or system design (if applicable)
